summary: Georgia list places a tower point labelled 'china hill' (GA242) in Telfair County; a separate report describes a Telfair tower that may or may not be this one.

evidence.supports: List entry GA242 at the coordinates, in Telfair County, with an elevation and no structure details
Names for towers numbered 73 and above are the compiler's own creation
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: List entry GA054, Telfair Lookout Tower, at 31.95351,-82.93348
China Hill is an unincorporated community in Telfair County
evidence.quote: China Hill is an unincorporated community in Telfair County , in the U.S. state of Georgia .

evidence.supports: A post office called Chinahill operated from 1876 to 1904
evidence.quote: A post office called Chinahill was established in 1876, and remained in operation until 1904.

evidence.supports: The community was named for a grove of chinaberry trees near the original town site
evidence.quote: The community was named for a grove of chinaberry trees near the original town site.

evidence.supports: A road realignment splits off from US 441/SR 31 around the Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower
evidence.quote: splits off from US 441/SR 31 to the east, around the Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower

evidence.supports: The tower is described as National Register eligible and the realignment aims to minimize impacts to it
evidence.quote: The purpose of the proposed road realignment is to minimize impacts to the National Register eligible Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower due to the widening of US 441/SR 31.

sources.title: Phase I, US 441/SR 31 Firetower Realignment, Telfair County, Georgia

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the UGA archaeology abstract describes a Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower near US 441/SR 31 as National Register eligible, but gives no location or date, and the page body was empty so the full report (possibly a PDF) was not read. The list's GA054 Telfair Lookout Tower (BLL and gfc tags) is about 16 km from the China Hill point; it is a plausible match for the UGA tower but no source links them, so the story does not. Neither the NHLR Georgia list nor the FFLOS Georgia former-sites list names a China Hill tower. Not used: a LinkedIn post (Pano AI) about a smoke detection near China Hill in Telfair County on April 7 (year unclear, page not read) that does not mention a tower. Build date, design, height, staffing, fate and the site today are unknown. Two searches were used; the Wikipedia community page is a stub.
